title: Signed Wire applications are deployed through one host-owned admission lifecycle
summary: Signed .wapp package or signed directory admission converges on Queue Fabric submission and a trusted ooRexx hosted deployment manager. HTTPS routes, Wire semantic application registration and gateway access-point publication are activated by generation, not manually wired into business code.
invariants: Verify Ed25519 signature, manifest digest, target policy, dependencies and approved entry factory before any activation; the Intention conversation resolves target but cannot bypass authorisation.
Share exactly the existing ObjectQueueManager; the gateway and browser cannot create arbitrary Queue Fabric clients or invent business state.
Static HTTPS routes remain immutable. Deployment publication is owner/generation CAS; route is published last, after semantic app and gateway are ready.
Web, Swing, GTK/Direct Linux and Android consume the same semantic definitions, revisions, actions, observation and ResourceRef authority.
Returning STAGED must never be equated with ACTIVE; completion requires live probe evidence.
Upgrade only deployment-owned app IDs; access-point migration needs controlled session drain and stale-revision rejection.
Queue Fabric ACK occurs after durable admission/rejection disposition; release when the journal fails.
No application-specific HTTP business API or second client-side state machine is introduced.
procedure: Stage and authenticate the signed .wapp and dependencies using trusted Crypto/Deployment.
Resolve target, mount, gateway profile and approvals through Intentions and policy.
Prove app readiness and provision fixed Queue Fabric gateway using existing manager.
Publish gateway binding, application generation and finally HTTPS route; restore prior generations if publication fails.
Record live TLS/browser probe separately and drain retired generation safely before removal.
